questions.prompt: A function has four if branches and none of them matches. What does it return?
choices: The last value it worked out
questions.explain: Falling off the end of a function returns None. A branch you forgot shows up as None reaching the caller, not as an error at the point of the mistake.

questions.prompt: Why give a calculator function an operation parameter instead of writing four separate functions?
choices: The caller can choose the operation at run time, including from user input
Python does not allow four similar functions
questions.explain: A value can be decided while the program runs; a function name in the source cannot. Passing the operation in is what lets the choice come from a user.

questions.prompt: Which of these make a function easier for someone else to use?
choices: A docstring saying what it returns
Parameter names that say what they hold
Returning a value rather than printing it
Doing as many unrelated jobs as possible in one function
questions.explain: The first three tell the caller what the deal is and leave them in charge of the result. A function that does several unrelated jobs can only be used when you want all of them.

questions.prompt: Match each piece of a well-built function to the job it does.
right: keeps one step small and separately named
explains the function to whoever calls it
hands the result back to the caller
lets a caller leave an option out
questions.explain: Each one solves a different problem: explaining, simplifying the call, simplifying the body, and delivering the answer.
